story: My salary for October 2026 (Rs 40,000) is unpaid. Section 12Z of the Code on Wages says I get double salary as penalty, right? Please confirm.

timeline.event: Salary for October 2026 became due but was not paid
timeline.user_words: My salary for October 2026 (Rs 40,000) is unpaid

facts.user_goal: Confirm if Section 12Z of the Code on Wages entitles them to double salary as penalty for non-payment of October 2026 salary

rules.name: monthly_due_date
rules.message: Wages for October 2026 were due before the end of 07 November 2026 (the 7th of the next month).
rules.label: When wages were due

rules.name: wage_claim_limitation
rules.message: File your wage claim before 07 Nov 2029 (1095 days left). This counts 3 years from 07 Nov 2026 (when October 2026 wages fell due; each later month has its own, later deadline). Don't wait for the last date.
rules.label: Last date to file your wage claim

rules.name: where_to_claim
rules.message: You (or your union) can file a claim before the wage authority. For banks, railways, telecom, mines, insurance and central PSUs this is the Central Government's authority; for other employers it is your State labour department. It can order up to ten times the claim as compensation and recovers unpaid amounts like land revenue. The employer has to prove they paid you.
rules.label: Where to claim

rules.name: amount
rules.message: Unpaid wages: 1 month(s) x Rs 40,000 = Rs 40,000 (before any lawful deductions; HRA and overtime also count as wages for payment).
rules.label: Amount

support.text: Your unpaid salary of Rs 40,000 is due before 07 November 2026.
support.reason: The law text does not specify Rs 40,000 or the date 07 November 2026. For monthly basis employees, wages must be paid before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month. The sentence adds a specific amount and date not contained in the law.

support.text: You can file a wage claim within 3 years from 07 November 2029.
support.reason: The law text states claims may be filed within three years from the date the claim arises, not from 07 November 2029. The sentence adds a specific date (07 November 2029) that is not in the law and does not follow from the law's general rule.

support.text: You can file a wage claim within 3 years from 07 November 2029.
support.reason: The law text states 'Three years When the wages accrue due' - this directly supports the sentence that a wage claim can be filed within 3 years from when wages accrue due. The sentence applies the law to a specific date (07 November 2029) which is acceptable as it is the user's own computed date.

support.text: The employer must prove they paid you if you file a claim for non-payment.
support.reason: The law text explicitly states 'the burden to prove that the said dues have been paid shall be on the employer' in cases of non-payment of wages or bonus. This directly supports the sentence.

Date: 08 November 2026
From: [FILL: your full name], [FILL: your full postal address]
To: [FILL: name of the other party], [FILL: their address / registered office / email]

Subject: Demand for payment of unpaid wages

I was employed with you at a monthly wage of Rs 40,000. My wages for October 2026 have not been paid.

I request you to pay the unpaid amount of Rs 40,000 within 15 days of receiving this letter, to my bank account [FILL: account details].

If the amount is not paid, I intend to file a claim before the authority under the Code on Wages, 2019, which may also award compensation, without further notice to you.

I have the following records: [FILL: receipts, chats, emails, bank statements].

Yours faithfully,
[FILL: your name and signature]

draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in your offer letter, salary slip, or the company's registered office on the MCA website (mca.gov.in).
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Code on Wages, 2019, s.17(1)-(4) (Time limit for payment of wages); Code on Wages, 2019, s.45(1)-(6) (Claims authority, compensation, recovery and time limit); Code on Wages, 2019, s.59 (Burden of proof on employer); Code on Wages, 2019, s.2(d) (Central or State Government: whose authority applies); Code on Wages, 2019, s.2(y) (main part, clauses (a)-(j)) (What counts as "wages")
